surveyDefinition.title: Organic Milk — consumer survey (Latin America)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Organic Milk. Every question asks about Organic Milk specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Latin America actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Latin America who buy or use Organic Milk for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. Excluded: Institutional buyers (restaurants, cafeterias, schools); Dairy farmers or processors; People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives.
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Organic milk is a retail grocery product purchased by households for personal consumption, making it a clear B2C market.
respondentBehaviours: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with organic milk, then moves through the occasions, household roles, frequency, and motivations that define their usage. It then traces the purchase journey from triggers and discovery through channels, restock cycles, decision drivers, spend, and routine. Next, it explores product expectations from must-haves and quality cues to packaging, claims, trade-offs, and value. Finally, it closes with satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, advocacy, and future intent, ending on the most forward-looking and sensitive topics.

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Organic Milk in Latin America — who Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. The consumer audience for organic milk is defined by household grocery shoppers who prioritize health, sustainability, and product quality, and who actively choose organic over conventional milk.

behaviors: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
exclusions: People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives

contextDemographics.geography: Urban and suburban areas with access to specialty grocery stores

assumptions: Organic milk is assumed to be a retail product, not a bulk ingredient
Consumers are assumed to be in regions where organic milk is widely available
The survey targets the end consumer, not retailers or distributors

options: Every day or almost every day
A few times in the month

A few times in the month

questions.insight: Top response: Several times a week (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mainstream Health Family, Conscious Parents, and Urban Health-Conscious Millennials drive frequent consumption; price-sensitive and rural personas skew to occasional or non-use.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, in which of the following situations was organic dairy milk consumed or served in your household? Select all that apply.

In cooking or baking (sauces, pancakes, etc.)

data.label: In coffee, tea, or hot chocolate
As a drink by itself (glass of milk)
In cooking or baking (sauces, pancakes, etc.)

questions.insight: Top response: As a drink by itself (glass of milk) (60.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family-oriented personas (Mainstream Health Family, Conscious Parents, Affluent Eco-Family) drive cereal and children's meals; Urban Millennials and Digital Natives boost smoothies and coffee use.

options: No one in the household drinks it regularly

data.label: No one in the household drinks it regularly

questions.insight: Top response: Adults (18 or older) (80.00%).

questions.question: In the last 30 days, how many glasses (8 oz each) of organic dairy milk did you or your household consume in a typical week?
questions.insight: Top response: 1 to 4 glasses per week (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Moderate consumption (1-9 glasses) dominates due to price sensitivity and occasional use; heavy consumption is driven by large families and health-focused households.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following reasons led you to choose organic dairy milk over conventional milk? Select all that apply.
options: I want milk without hormones and antibiotics

data.label: I want milk without hormones and antibiotics

questions.insight: Top response: Health and nutrition benefits (70.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health and hormone-free are top drivers across all personas; environmental and animal welfare are stronger among Eco-Activists, Affluent Eco-Family, and Wellness Empty Nesters.

questions.question: How important is it to you that the organic dairy milk you buy is produced without hormones and antibiotics?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Most personas highly value hormone/antibiotic-free production; only price-focused traditional buyers place lower importance.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following most often triggered your purchase of organic dairy milk?

A promotional offer or discount at the store

I saw it in the store and decided to buy it
A planned restock on my regular shopping day

questions.insight: Top response: A health concern or dietary need in my household (34.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-driven personas (Mainstream Health Family, Conscious Parent, Rural Health Advocate) plus price-sensitive segments (Price-Sensitive Traditional Buyer) drive health and promotion triggers.

questions.question: Before buying organic dairy milk, where do you typically look for information or compare options? Select all that apply.
options: I don't usually look for information before buying

data.label: I don't usually look for information before buying

questions.insight: Top response: In-store labels and packaging (62.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Laggard and mainstream personas rely on in-store labels and word-of-mouth; digital natives and millennials add online channels.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, where did you buy organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: Farmers' market or direct from farm

data.label: Farmers' market or direct from farm

questions.insight: Top response: Large supermarket or hypermarket (68.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mainstream and price-sensitive personas favor large supermarkets; eco and rural personas add farmers' markets; digital natives add online.

questions.question: When you buy organic dairy milk, how much do you typically purchase at one time?
options: Two to three bottles or cartons
Four or more bottles or cartons
It varies from trip to trip

data.label: Two to three bottles or cartons
Four or more bottles or cartons
It varies from trip to trip

questions.insight: Top response: Two to three bottles or cartons (48.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family-oriented personas buy in larger quantities; singles and trialists buy one or vary.

questions.question: When you are at the store choosing organic dairy milk, how important is each of the following factors in your decision? (Please rate each one separately)
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health and clean-label motivations across most personas push importance toward high end; price-sensitive segments temper extremes.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, approximately how much did your household spend in total on organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: $10 to $19 (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Middle-income personas cluster in $10-$29; affluent eco and premium personas push higher spend.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how you decide to buy organic dairy milk?
options: I buy it on a set schedule without thinking much about it
I buy it whenever I run out, without comparing other options
I buy it when it is on promotion or at a good price
I reconsider each time whether organic dairy milk is worth it
I buy it only when I find a brand or product I trust

data.label: I buy it on a set schedule without thinking much about it
I buy it whenever I run out, without comparing other options
I buy it when it is on promotion or at a good price
I reconsider each time whether organic dairy milk is worth it
I buy it only when I find a brand or product I trust

questions.insight: Top response: I buy it when it is on promotion or at a good price (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Price-sensitive and mainstream personas drive promotion and reconsideration; loyal personas (Rural, Eco-Activist) drive trust-based buying.

questions.question: Which of the following would you consider a non-negotiable requirement when buying organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones)
No added sugar or artificial ingredients
Consistent taste and texture from one purchase to the next
Milk from cows that are pasture-raised or grass-fed

data.label: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones)
No added sugar or artificial ingredients
Consistent taste and texture from one purchase to the next
Milk from cows that are pasture-raised or grass-fed

questions.insight: Top response: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones) (72.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health and clean-label motivations dominate; eco and animal welfare personas add pasture-raised; lactose-free is niche.

questions.question: How important is it to you that the organic dairy milk you buy has a clearly visible organic certification label on the front of the package?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mainstream Health Family, Conscious Parent, and Rural Health Advocate strongly value clear certification; Eco-Activist and Wellness-Seeking also push toward high importance. Only a small share of price-focused or convenience-driven personas downplay it.

questions.question: Which of the following packaging features would be most important to you when buying organic dairy milk?
options: Longer shelf life (e.g., UHT or extended fresh)
Clear/transparent packaging to see the milk

data.label: Longer shelf life (e.g., UHT or extended fresh)
Clear/transparent packaging to see the milk

questions.insight: Top response: Longer shelf life (e.g., UHT or extended fresh) (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Shelf life is top concern for Convenience-Driven, Urban Millennial, and Empty Nester due to spoilage pain point. Family personas prefer larger sizes; Eco-Activist and Affluent Eco-Family push eco-friendly packaging.

questions.question: Which of the following claims or certifications would most increase your trust in an organic dairy milk product? Select all that apply.
options: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification

data.label: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification

questions.insight: Top response: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification (62.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Clear organic certification is a top trust driver across most personas. Grass-fed and local claims resonate with health, eco, and rural personas. Non-GMO and animal welfare have moderate support; carbon-neutral is niche.

questions.question: If you could not find an organic dairy milk that meets all your preferences, which trade-off would you be most willing to make?
options: Pay a higher price for a product that meets all my other preferences
Accept a less convenient package size or format
Choose a product with fewer sustainability or animal-welfare claims
Choose a product with a less consistent taste or texture
Choose a product with a shorter shelf life

data.label: Pay a higher price for a product that meets all my other preferences
Accept a less convenient package size or format
Choose a product with fewer sustainability or animal-welfare claims
Choose a product with a less consistent taste or texture

questions.insight: Top response: I would not be willing to make any trade-off (25.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Price-sensitive personas (Traditional, Family, Rural) are more willing to give up sustainability claims to save money. Premium and eco personas are less willing to trade off, hence higher 'no trade-off'. Some affluent will pay more.

questions.question: How much more would you be willing to pay for organic dairy milk compared to conventional dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Up to 10% more (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: High price sensitivity across many personas caps willingness to pay. Most accept up to 10-25% premium. Affluent and premium personas drive the tail of higher willingness.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied are you with the organic dairy milk you currently buy?

questions.distributionNote: Mixed sentiment due to price and availability issues. Loyal and affluent personas are more satisfied; price-sensitive and convenience-driven are less so. Many are moderately satisfied but not fully.

metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with organic milk, then moves through the occasions, household roles, frequency, and motivations that define their usage. It then traces the purchase journey from triggers and discovery through channels, restock cycles, decision drivers, spend, and routine. Next, it explores product expectations from must-haves and quality cues to packaging, claims, trade-offs, and value. Finally, it closes with satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, advocacy, and future intent, ending on the most forward-looking and sensitive topics.
storyline_notes: Adapted for a perishable consumable: added a 'restock cycle' beat in buying_behavior and emphasized shelf-life concerns in format/packaging and friction.

Regional adaptation: given high price sensitivity and limited availability in Latin America, 'spend' and 'availability' are woven into decision drivers and friction, but spend remains late in its section.
Added a 'discovery and information' beat that includes how shoppers verify organic claims, reflecting the pain point of unclear certification in the region.
In consumer_profile, placed 'household involvement' before 'usage frequency' to capture the family decision dynamic early, which is important for a family-oriented market.
No replacement/upgrade beat, as it does not apply to a consumable.
Kept all beats answerable with closed questions and avoided age, income, geography, and brand names.
metadata.classification_reason: Organic milk is a retail grocery product purchased by households for personal consumption, making it a clear B2C market.
